title: Research agenda
description: What we intend to research for one contest: an editorial work list, not a factual claim, so it carries no citations. Fixed BEFORE research starts so that every candidate is asked the same questions. `npm run next` diffs the agenda against verified data to produce a deterministic task queue. References here may point at records that do not exist yet. Path: data/agenda/<election-slug>/<contest-slug>.json

candidates.description: People to research for an office contest (empty for measures). These are seeds: candidacy is only verified once the contest file cites the official certified list.

questions.description: Issue questions every candidate is researched on.

measures.description: Ballot measures every candidate is researched on (stance support/oppose/...).

finance_cutoff.description: Last day of the filing period to pull money data through. The SAME cutoff applies to every candidate (parity). null = not chosen yet (`npm run next` emits a task to choose it).

exhausted.description: Count-based tasks (endorsements, contributions, independent expenditures, measure committees) that cannot reach their target because no more exist. Each entry closes one task id from `npm run next` and records where we looked.

office_ref.description: The office this contest elects (office contests). Editorial link; may point at a record research has not created yet.

vote_for.description: Office contests: how many candidates each voter may choose, which is also how many seats the contest fills ("Vote for 3" on the ballot). Omitted means 1 or not yet known. Set only when an official source states it; seeded.note says which source and whether it was opened. The contest record's vote_for, once it cites the official list, takes precedence.

promise_topics.description: Editorial topics that group candidates' campaign promises for this contest, so the site can show which topics several candidates address and which only one does. Topics describe what a promise is about, never a stance or its quality; each promise names one topic id in its dossier item (`topic`).
